correctness.rationale: A positive-discriminant quadratic yields precisely two positive subunit roots. Vieta and hyperbolic addition give exact total-depth recovery and the density-scaled product. Differentiation of the ratio gives a strictly positive sign because coth(t)-t csch²(t) is strictly increasing; endpoint limits give the complete realizability interval and unique inverse. Reconstructing both sum and product suffices to recover the measured roots, and a one-wavenumber continuum establishes minimality. A separate standard-library program passed 600 seeded forward/inverse cases, equal-depth checks, and arbitrary depth-reflection tests; finite testing is not treated as the proof.

value.rationale: The exact identifiability of density contrast and layer partition from a minimal set of paired surface/internal wave frequencies is a natural inverse problem. The result provides a globally valid feasibility test and algorithm, distinguishes which physical data are fundamentally insufficient, and identifies an unavoidable all-wavenumber isospectral ambiguity, useful when designing measurements. No noise robustness is implied.
